ru-imperial.title: Flag of the Russian Empire

colors.note: The double-headed eagle of the Romanov dynasty.
The golden field of the imperial arms.
Purity and the Russian Orthodox tradition.

desc:
- The Russian Empire's official flag (1858–1917) was a black-yellow-white tricolour
- The more familiar white-blue-red merchant flag was also widely used
- **Construction:** three equal horizontal bands of black (top), yellow (middle), and white (bottom)
- Used as the national flag of the Russian Empire from 1858 to 1896, then replaced by the white-blue-red tricolour
trivia:
- The Imperial Russian flag represented the Russian Empire until the 1917 revolution
- The white-blue-red colours became the basis for modern Russian flag
- Established by Peter the Great

ru-sfsr.title: Flag of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic

colors.note: Communist revolution and the workers' struggle.

desc:
- The flag of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic was a red field bearing the Cyrillic letters 'РСФСР' (or, in later versions, the hammer and sickle with a blue vertical stripe at the hoist)
- The RSFSR was the largest and most populous republic of the USSR (1917–1991)
- Its flag went through several redesigns; the final 1954 version featured a red field with a light blue vertical stripe at the hoist and the hammer-sickle-star in the upper corner
- **Construction:** a red field with a light blue vertical stripe occupying one-eighth of the flag at the hoist
- The hammer, sickle, and star in the upper-hoist corner
- Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- The Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR) was the largest Soviet republic
- The hammer and sickle represented communist ideology
- Became the Russian Federation after the Soviet Union collapsed

soviet-union.title: Flag of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

colors.note: The blood of workers and the communist revolution.

desc:
- A red field with a golden hammer and sickle beneath a gold-bordered red star in the upper hoist corner
- Adopted on 12 November 1923, the flag symbolised the unity of industrial workers (hammer) and peasant farmers (sickle) under communist leadership (the star)
- It flew over the USSR for nearly seven decades until 25 December 1991
- The red represented the blood of workers' struggle; the gold symbolised a bright communist future. One of the 20th century's most recognisable flags
- **Construction:** a red field with the hammer and sickle centred in the upper-hoist quarter. The red star is above the emblem. Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- The hammer and sickle was originally designed by artist Yevgeny Kamzolkin as a logo for a May Day parade in 1918
- The hammer represents industrial workers; the sickle represents farmers
- The Soviet flag inspired communist flags worldwide and was iconic for an entire political ideology
